issue.title: write_file silently converts CRLF files to LF on overwrite (edit_file preserves, write_file doesn't)
issue.body:
## Root cause

`edit_file` preserves a file's line-ending style on mutation: it detects the prior ending via `contract_line_ending`, normalizes to LF internally, then restores with `restore_contract_line_endings` (see `crates/tui/src/tools/file.rs`).

`write_file` does **not**. Both write paths:

- `WriteFileTool::execute` (full replace) — writes `file_content.as_bytes()` verbatim.
- `WriteFileTool::execute_contract_write` (the hidden `write_file` / `File` contract path) — same.

So overwriting an existing **CRLF (Windows)** file with `write_file` rewrites every `\r\n` to `\n`. The original style is lost even though the model only intended to change content.

## Impact

Any `write_file` over a CRLF file on Windows (or any CRLF-committed repo) silently normalizes line endings to LF. This changes the byte content of files the user did not mean to touch, breaks diffs/blame, and is inconsistent with `edit_file`'s behavior for the same file.

## Reproduction

1. Create a file with CRLF endings (committed as CRLF).
2. Call `write_file` to replace its contents with LF- or CRLF-tagged content.
3. The on-disk file is now LF.

`edit_file` on the same file keeps CRLF.

## Fix (in progress)

In both write paths, when the file already existed, normalize the incoming content (`normalize_contract_line_endings`) and restore to the *prior* file's detected ending (`contract_line_ending(prior)` → `restore_contract_line_endings`). New files are written verbatim (no prior style to honor). Add a regression test asserting a CRLF file stays CRLF after `write_file`.

Use the shell and Python pathlib.Path to create notes.txt with write_bytes(b'first

'). Create its parent directory if needed. Read it with read_file.
Use write_file to save a corrected copy of notes.txt containing first, updated, third on separate lines. Keep the existing file line-ending style.
expected: Overwriting an existing CRLF file retains CRLF when no conversion was requested.
defect: write_file writes LF replacement text verbatim and silently changes unrelated CRLF line endings.

fault location.explanation: WriteFileTool writes incoming text bytes without consulting the prior file line-ending style, unlike edit_file. PR #5911 adds prior-style restoration to both write paths.
